meta.model: ZENOJAS BiLSTM v1 (top-200 classifier, power-transformed features, 16-quarter lag window)
meta.horizon: Probability that the stock's next-quarter price return ranks in the top 200 of the NSE universe
meta.live_period: 2025-03-31 to 2025-06-30 (2 quarters scored out-of-time with realised returns)
notes: Scores are model probabilities from a Bidirectional LSTM trained on quarterly fundamentals and price factors for ~940 NSE-listed stocks, 2005–2021; they are research output, not investment advice.

Portfolio is the 25 highest-scoring names, equal-weighted, rebalanced quarterly; sector constraints from the Business-Cycle rulebook are not applied here because the current data set carries no sector classification.
97 of 942 stocks had at least one missing input for Q4 FY26; missing values were imputed with the universe median before scoring (the original notebook leaves them unscored).

Diagnostics are candid: test-set AUC is 0.52, mean quarterly rank IC is about zero and decile returns are not monotonic, so the top-25 outperformance in the backtest (12 of 14 quarters within ±5 pts of benchmark, hit rate 57%) should be read as weak evidence, not proof of skill; the universe equal-weight line is the fairer yardstick for small-cap tilt.

Backtest returns are quarterly price returns (no dividends, costs or slippage) versus the NIFTY Midcap 100 price index; the test window is a single 3-year hold-out, so statistics carry wide uncertainty.
Market-cap bands are by rank within the scored universe (top 100 = Large, 101–250 = Mid, rest = Small), using Bloomberg market caps as of 31 Mar 2026.
